newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Semiconductor plans $14.5 bln facilities.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Semiconductor plans $14.5 bln facilities.

text.p: Taiwan's top chipmaker said on Thursday it planned a massive investment in southern Taiwan, and analysts said the move was the only way the firm could keep its lead in the highly competitive semiconductor industry.
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp said in a statement that it would invest T$400 billion (US$14.5 billion) in the Tainan Science-based Industrial Park in southern Taiwan over the next 10 years.
The planned facilities would include a T$80 billion wafer-fabrication plant to make 12-inch semiconductors and a T$40 billion fabrication plant to make 8-inch wafers.
The Tainan investment would be Taiwan's largest single industrial project -- bigger even than Formosa group's huge T$240 billion (US$9 billion) petrochemical plant at Yunlin in the south.
Analysts said the investment was necessary for the chipmaker to stay ahead amid fierce international competition. Prices of semiconductors have plummeted recently due to a world supply glut.
"As a foundry, Taiwan Semiconductor needs to constantly move forward in terms of technology and capacity," said Julia Teng, analyst for Baring Securities. "This is only way to survive."
Alex Chen of Wardley James Capel said the investment was feasible but there are lots of uncertainties in the ever-changing industry.
"The company has provided a grand vision, but the future is too difficult to predict," Chen said.
"The general view right now is the semiconductor industry will remain the star sector (worldwide) until 2010. But nobody can predict what the industry will look like at that time," he said.

Taiwan Semiconductor said it expected the global microchip market to grow to US$300 billion by 2000, with demand soaring for chip-based three-dimensional multimedia, ISDN, high-speed modems, digital video, digital television equipment and digital telephones, mobile phones and cameras.
But the company's committment to build a 12-inch wafer fab raised analysts' eyebrows.
"Investment in the 12-inch wafer fab requires huge capital, and investment return is a big question mark," Chen said.
Taiwan Semiconductor's project gives a significant boost to the fledgling Tainan facility, a new southern rival to Taiwan's main high-technology manufacturing park at Hsinchu in the north.
Taiwan Semiconductor president Donald Brooks said his firm was "moving energetically to bring its long-term investment plans in line with the national policy of developing southern Taiwan".
The Tainan Science-based Industrial Park (TSIP) is scheduled to start operation in 1998.
"The T$400 billion, 10-year TSIP Manufacturing Centre project has been carefully formulated and will be carried out step by step," Brooks said in the statement.

"Because of its efficient organisation, plentiful land and high-quality human resources, Tainan Science-based Industrial Park is the best possible location for (Taiwan Semiconductor) to expand its manufacturing facilities," Brooks added.
Taiwan Semiconductor's cluster of wafer fabs and research and development facilities would employ 5,000 people -- more than the firm's current 4,300-strong workforce.

Taiwan's top chipmaker operates two six-inch wafer fabs and two eight-inch wafer fabs in Taiwan. A third eight-inch fab is under construction in Taiwan and a fourth in the United States through a joint venture, it said.
